questions.text: A graph is self-complementary if it is isomorphic to its complement. For all self-complementary graphs on n vertices, n is
questions.solution:
A graph and its complement have equal edges, so each has half of [latex]\binom n2[/latex]: [latex]\frac{n(n-1)}{4}[/latex] must be an integer.

This holds only when n [latex]\equiv[/latex] 0 or 1 (mod 4).

Answer: Congruent to 0 mod 4, or 1 mod 4

questions.text: In a connected graph, a bridge is an edge whose removal disconnects a graph. Which one of the following statements is true?
questions.solution:
If an edge were on a cycle, the rest of the cycle would still connect its ends after removing it, so it would not be a bridge.

- Every edge of a tree is a bridge.
- Clique edges (size [latex]\ge[/latex] 3) lie on triangles, so they are not bridges.
- A graph can have both bridges and cycles.

Answer: A bridge cannot be part of a simple cycle

Every edge of a clique with size [latex]\geq[/latex] 3 is a bridge (A clique is any complete subgraph of a graph)
A graph with bridges cannot have a cycle

questions.text: Which one of the following well formed formulae is a tautology?
questions.solution:
Option 3: [latex]P\rightarrow R\equiv\neg P\vee R[/latex], and both sides apply the same quantifiers to equivalent formulas [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] tautology.

- Option 1: [latex]\forall x\exists y[/latex] does not imply [latex]\exists y\forall x[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not a tautology.
- Option 2: fails, e.g. when nothing satisfies R.

Note: option 4 is also logically valid (the bound variables are only renamed). The official key is option 3.

Answer: Option 3

questions.text: Which one of the following assertions concerning code inspection and code walkthrough is true?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Inspection is done before unit testing [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] option 1 false.
- Inspection (formal, checklist based) and walkthrough (informal, led by the author) are different [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] option 2 false.
- Inspections check against checklists including coding standards [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True.
- Walkthroughs are done by the development team, not an independent test team [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] false.

Answer: Adherence to coding standards is checked during code inspection

questions.text: A half adder is implemented with XOR and AND gates. A full Combinational Circuit is implemented with two half Combinational Circuits and one OR gate. The propagation delay of an XOR gate is twice that of an AND/OR gate. The propagation delay of an AND/OR gate is 1.2 microseconds. A 4-bit ripple-carry binary Combinational Circuit is implemented by using four full Combinational Circuits. The total propagation time of this 4-bit binary Combinational Circuit in microseconds is____________.
questions.solution:
XOR = 2.4 [latex]\mu s[/latex], AND = OR = 1.2 [latex]\mu s[/latex].

Carry out of one full adder: XOR (first half adder) + AND (second half adder) + OR = 2.4 + 1.2 + 1.2 = 4.8 [latex]\mu s[/latex].

Taking each of the 4 ripple stages as 4.8 [latex]\mu s[/latex]: 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 4.8 = 19.2 [latex]\mu s[/latex] (as per the official key).

Answer: 19.2
